Canceling HTTP requests with context

Every outgoing request in Go can carry a context.Context. Create the request with
http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, method, url, body) and pass a context that you can
cancel. When the context is canceled or its deadline passes, the transport aborts the
connection and client.Do returns an error that wraps context.Canceled or
context.DeadlineExceeded.

    ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
    defer cancel()
    req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, "https://example.com", nil)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)

Always call cancel, even when the request succeeds, so the timer is released. To stop
a request from another goroutine, keep the cancel function and call it there. Reading
the response body also honours the context: a body read after cancellation fails.
